S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

info.persona: Lois Vassar balances a quiet love of solitary creativity with a disciplined professional drive, punctuated by a habit of late‑night crossword puzzles and an unwavering commitment to ethical advertising.
info.professional_persona: Lois Vassar, an advertising sales strategist with a foundation in education, blends data‑driven market analysis with pedagogical insight, using their collaborative, detail‑oriented nature to craft ethically grounded campaigns for learning‑focused clients while maintaining a calm, humility‑driven office presence.
info.cultural_background: Lois was raised in a midwestern, white‑American family in Omaha, Nebraska. Her upbringing emphasized modesty, self‑reliance, and a strong sense of community—a hallmark of the region’s cultural fabric. Family gatherings and local traditions fostered a respect for quiet, reflective spaces and an appreciation for the natural landscape of the Great Plains. Growing up, she internalized Midwestern values of straightforward communication, humility, and a collaborative spirit, which now influence her professional etiquette and personal relationships. While she identifies with mainstream American cultural norms, she also embraces the region’s understated humor and the value placed on balancing work responsibilities with personal well‑being.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Lois gravitates toward solitary and quiet pursuits that feed her curiosity while allowing her to recharge. She enjoys reading non‑fiction books on educational psychology and cultural studies, which satisfy her love of new ideas without the pressure of social settings. Regular nature walks and birdwatching in the Nebraska countryside provide a meditative backdrop for reflection. She is an avid photographer, capturing subtle moments in landscapes and architecture. Creative writing—short stories, poetry, and journaling—offers an outlet for personal expression. Lois also finds solace in knitting, puzzle solving (crosswords and Sudoku), and digital art, often creating illustrations on her tablet. Occasionally, she mentors individual students online, offering one‑on‑one tutoring that aligns with her cooperative nature while maintaining low‑key interaction.
info.sports_persona: Lois Vassar enjoys solitary nature walks and weekly trail runs, is an active member of the Omaha Birding Club, follows the Nebraska Cornhuskers football team and the Omaha Storm Chasers baseball club with a quiet, Saturday‑morning devotion, and incorporates a disciplined yoga routine to maintain flexibility and core strength.
info.arts_persona: Lois Vassar, an avid photographer and digital illustrator, draws inspiration from Ansel Adams’s landscapes, the lyrical minimalism of Sufjan Stevens, and the subtle brushwork of Georgia O’Keeffe, frequently visiting the Joslyn Art Museum and curating a personal collection of black‑and‑white prints that capture Nebraska’s quiet horizons.
info.travel_persona: Lois Vassar prefers off‑season, self‑planned trips that blend solitude with natural wonder, having trekked the limestone bluffs of Badlands National Park, explored Iceland’s volcanic fields, and sampled local farm‑to‑table experiences in Tuscany, while dreaming of a quiet retreat in the Scottish Highlands where they can photograph mist‑shrouded lochs.
info.culinary_persona: Lois Vassar enjoys wholesome, home‑cooked meals with a penchant for seasonal Midwestern produce, often preparing roasted chicken with heirloom carrots, a beet‑goat‑cheese salad, and hand‑kneaded sourdough bread, while their modest cooking skill level is punctuated by an occasional attempt at wild‑mushroom risotto and a love for a well‑balanced espresso.

info.persona: Willie Ollins, a 40‑year‑old construction leader with a restless imagination, balances relentless project precision with late‑night art‑themed cooking sessions, while a chronic habit of over‑analyzing schedules fuels both executive ambition and occasional stress‑induced insomnia, a pattern they struggle to quiet.
info.professional_persona: Willie Ollins, a 40-year-old construction project manager in Los Angeles, leverages meticulous budgeting, BIM expertise, and a flair for artistic design to drive large mixed-use developments while channeling their imaginative curiosity into sustainable, community-focused builds.
info.cultural_background: Willie was raised in a close‑knit African‑American community in South Los Angeles, where family gatherings, church events, and neighborhood block parties fostered a strong sense of cultural identity. He celebrates traditions such as Juneteenth and Kwanzaa, incorporating soulful music, storytelling, and classic Southern cuisine into his life. His upbringing instilled an appreciation for resilience and collective progress, which he channels into his professional commitment to increasing representation of black professionals in construction. Willie actively participates in local black trade associations and community development initiatives, using his cultural perspective to advocate for inclusive design, equitable housing, and mentorship opportunities for underrepresented youth.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Willie immerses himself in the vibrant LA art scene, attending gallery openings, street‑art tours, and live music events ranging from jazz to hip‑hop. He practices urban photography, capturing architectural details and community life, and enjoys painting mural concepts for personal projects. His sociable nature leads him to play pickup basketball and organize weekend group hikes. He also explores culinary experimentation, especially blending Southern soul food with Asian flavors, and participates in cooking workshops. To balance his stress sensitivity, he practices yoga and guided meditation, and he volunteers with local mentoring programs that introduce youth to construction trades and creative design.
info.sports_persona: Willie Ollins, an energetic 40-year-old, shuttles between weekend hikes with the Los Angeles Hiking Club, pickup basketball games at Westside Hoops, and cheering for the LA Lakers and LA Galaxy, activities they use to counteract construction-site stress.
info.arts_persona: Willie Ollins immerses themselves in LA’s art pulse, attending openings at The Broad, joining street‑art tours featuring works by Shepard Fairey and Faith 47, and regularly catching live sets by jazz virtuoso Kamasi Washington and hip‑hop poet Kendrick Lamar, channeling this exposure into personal mural concepts.
info.travel_persona: Willie Ollins, a 40-year-old with a blend of meticulous trip planning and spontaneous curiosity, has road‑tripped the Pacific Coast Highway, explored Tokyo’s design districts and New Orleans’ music‑laden streets, and dreams of a design-focused pilgrimage to Barcelona’s modernist landmarks, a journey they hope to document through photography.
info.culinary_persona: Willie Ollins, an avid home chef, experiments at an intermediate level by fusing Southern staples—fried chicken, collard greens, and mac and cheese—with Asian umami via miso brines, gochujang glaze, and kimchi infusions, often showcasing creations like gochujang‑glazed collard greens atop buttery grits, dishes they share at neighborhood potlucks.

info.persona: Vanisha Bailey blends disciplined entrepreneurship with vibrant community spirit, juggling high‑standard laundry mastery, gospel leadership, and a relentless pursuit of sustainable success despite occasional stress‑driven splurges, and they keep a meticulous ledger of every receipt.
info.professional_persona: Vanisha Bailey is a veteran laundry and dry‑cleaning expert with over twenty years of experience, renowned for designing ultra‑efficient workflow layouts, mastering fabric‑specific stain removal, and delivering charismatic customer service workshops while leveraging their disciplined, competitive nature to drive high standards and mentor staff.
info.cultural_background: Vanisha is a second‑generation African‑American who grew up in a close‑knit Black neighbourhood of Los Angeles. Her family emphasized hard work, education, and community involvement, with frequent gatherings that celebrated gospel music, soul food, and storytelling. She draws strength from the resilience and creativity that characterize Black cultural heritage, and she stays connected to her roots through church activities, mentorship of younger Black women, and participation in local cultural festivals that honor African‑American history. Living in Woodland Hills, she blends this cultural identity with the diverse, multicultural environment of Los Angeles, valuing both tradition and the opportunities of her city.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Vanisha is a vibrant community member. She loves cooking soulful, health‑conscious meals and often hosts potluck gatherings for her church and neighborhood. Her voice shines in the gospel choir, where she enjoys leading songs and arranging harmonies. She participates in local theater productions, taking on both acting and backstage roles, and she dances socially—especially swing and line dancing—at community events. Gardening on her backyard patio provides a structured, calming hobby, while she also reads mystery novels and self‑help books to unwind. To manage stress, she practices gentle yoga and mindfulness meditation, and she volunteers weekly at a senior center, offering laundry assistance and companionship.
info.sports_persona: Vanisha Bailey enjoys social swing and line dancing at community gatherings, roots for the Los Angeles Dodgers and the LA Galaxy, and participates in weekly low‑impact Zumba classes at the senior center they volunteer at, balancing competitive team spirit with a love for rhythmic movement.
info.arts_persona: Vanisha Bailey shines as a lead vocalist and harmony arranger in their gospel choir, drawing inspiration from Kirk Franklin and Tasha Cobbs Leonard, while also acting and choreographing backstage for productions at the Woodland Hills Community Playhouse, and they never miss a mystery novel by Agatha Christie before bedtime.
info.travel_persona: Vanisha Bailey prefers road trips that blend nature and culture, having driven the Pacific Coast Highway to Santa Barbara, hiked in Big Bear Lake, and booked a weekend getaway to Sedona for its red‑rock scenery, while they dream of a future eco‑tourism retreat in Costa Rica once their boutique stabilizes.
info.culinary_persona: Vanisha Bailey crafts soulful, health‑focused meals like quinoa‑stuffed bell peppers, roasted sweet‑potato bisque, and turmeric‑infused grilled salmon, cooking with a practiced hand on their cast‑iron skillet and drizzling homemade herb‑infused olive oil, while their pantry is stocked with kale, chickpeas, and seasonal berries.
